'''Ryszard Syski''' (April 8, 1924 in [[Płock]], [[Poland]] - June 11, 2007 in [[Silver Spring, Maryland]]) was a [[Polish people|Polish]]-[[United States|American]] [[mathematician]] whose research was in [[queueing theory]].<ref>[http://www.hindawi.com/GetArticle.aspx?doi=10.1155/S1048953398000173 Editorial] of special issue, devoted to Syski,  Journal of Applied Mathematics and Stochastic Analysis Volume 11 (1998), Issue 3, Pages 219-220</ref>

During [[World War II]] he was in the [[Armia Krajowa]] with his parents, partaking in the [[Warsaw Uprising]], being imprisoned in [[Stalag VIII-B|Lamsdorf]], [[Silesia]] and [[Bavaria]] (1944), and joining the [[Polish Second Corps]] for fights in Italy (1945).

His studies in mathematics started in [[London]], at the [[Polish University Abroad]] (1946).  He
joined ''Automatic Telephone and Electric Co.'' in London (1952).
He got his [[B.Sc.]] (1954) and [[Ph.D.]] (1961) at [[University of London]], on the dissertation
''Stochastic Process in [[Banach space]] and its Applications to Congestion Theory''.<ref>{{cite thesis | url = http://encore.ulrls.lon.ac.uk/iii/encore/record/C__Rb2997489 | title = Stochastic process in Banach space and its applications to congestion theory | publisher = Senate House Libraries Catalogue | access-date = 13 February 2013 | last1 = Syski | first1 = R. }}</ref>

Encouraged by [[Thomas L. Saaty]] he moved to [[College Park, Maryland]], joining  the mathematics faculty of [[University of Maryland, College Park|University of Maryland]] (1961–1999), 
founded the journal [[Stochastic Processes and their Applications]] (1973) 
and was fellow of the Institute of Mathematical Statistics.  
Syski wrote over forty journal articles, often collaborating with notables such as
[[Felix Pollaczek|Félix Pollaczek]],
[[Lajos Takács]],
[[Julian Keilson]] and
[[Wim Cohen]].  
Syski died of complications from a brain injury received during a fall.<ref>[https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/07/05/AR2007070501913_pf.html obituary] in ''[[The Washington Post]]'' (July 6, 2007)</ref>

==Books==
*''Introduction to congestion theory in telephone systems'' ([[North-Holland Publishing Company|North-Holland]], 1960)
*''Passage times for [[Markov chain]]s'' (1992)
